result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk and a traffic signal, but it lacks modern pedestrian safety features. The environment is characterized by a multi-lane one-way street with parked cars that may obstruct sightlines and a lack of accessible infrastructure.

hazards.name: Missing Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The lack of sloped curb transitions at the crosswalk creates a significant barrier for pedestrians with mobility impairments or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground corners at the start of the crosswalk

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction from Parking
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk limit the visibility between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway near the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: While vehicle signals are present, there are no dedicated pedestrian signal heads to indicate when it is safe to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic signal pole on the right corner

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install concrete curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces to ensure the crossing is accessible to all users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear guidance on crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by 'daylighting' the intersection.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of continuous sidewalks and faded crossing infrastructure. Parked vehicles near the intersection create significant sightline obstructions, increasing risk for pedestrians in this residential setting.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection block the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs near the foreground crosswalk

hazards.name: Incomplete Sidewalk Network
hazards.description: The absence of a sidewalk on the left side of the street forces pedestrians into the roadway or onto unpaved surfaces.

hazards.name: Degraded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk is faded and difficult to see, reducing driver awareness of the crossing.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Apply thermoplastic continental markings to replace the faded transverse lines.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Install a standard concrete sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a continuous pedestrian path.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks, but lacks dedicated pedestrian signals. The presence of parked vehicles near the crossing and utility poles on the sidewalk creates minor visual and physical obstructions.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians must rely on vehicle traffic lights, which may not provide adequate clearance time or clear right-of-way indication.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners where signals are mounted.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street block the sight lines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to clarify when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals at a signalized junction in a mixed-use urban area. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment lacks advanced safety features like curb extensions or daylighting to protect pedestrians from turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners may obstruct the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs near the intersection corners.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.
